design_note: Deliberately a THIN-ENTITY event: neither arm could win on entity recall (3percentclub, Fractal NYC and Maria Ashby are blank in both). The intended discriminator was how each arm handles thinness — honest emptiness vs padding.

preference_note: Preference not stated explicitly; inferred because X dominates every criterion (5>4 usable, 0=0 errors, 5>3 non-obvious, yes>no changed). Correctable by Alex.

deciding_reason: Both packs handled thinness identically well (honest, unpadded, zero errors), so the tiebreaker was how much genuinely on-topic substance survived extraction. X pulled dated, numerically specific material for 2 of 3 topic cards, including the Cerebras/Qwen3.8 1500 tok/s figure landing inside tonight's compute-budget lab. Y won on one excellent reader-tailored item (the routed-answer verification question) but self-admits its topic material is off-target where it exists.
notes: Called it narrow. Noted that on 'single best line to say tonight' Y might edge it.

detail: Zero errors on both packs from both seats — neither arm padded under thinness, which was the designed test. The legacy arm won on density of on-topic substance.

event_dropped: ai-show-and-tell-ny (2026-09-20) — Alex did not attend; could not score criterion 1.
pre_registered_rule: B replaces A only if preferred-or-tied on BOTH events with <= errors; split -> third event; indistinguishable -> stop and rethink.
RULING: B DOES NOT REPLACE A. The substrate was not preferred-or-tied on both events: it lost event 2 on both seats and only took event 1 on one of two seats. The legacy Step 1.7a pull remains the prior-context retrieval path. ADR-10 stays PROPOSED, not Accepted — its acceptance was gated on this A/B.
interpretation_NOT_part_of_the_rule: Alex's two preferences split by EVENT TYPE, not randomly: he preferred the substrate on the entity-rich event (Apollo, where real continuity existed to retrieve) and the legacy pull on the thin event (AI Builders, where neither arm had entity coverage and Notion's topic records simply held more substance than the graph). That is a coherent pattern, and it suggests the comparison was partly a COVERAGE comparison rather than a METHOD comparison — the graph holds claims from post-event briefs, while Notion topic pages hold hand-curated depth accumulated over months. Recorded as interpretation, explicitly NOT used to soften the ruling above.
what_the_experiment_actually_bought: The durable finding is not which arm won. It is that the arms are good at different things — substrate on MATERIAL (Alex, Apollo: 'topic cards are far stronger'), legacy on PACKAGING (both seats, repeatedly: speaker-named chase-able questions, dated numerically-specific signals). That is what YED-217 (conditioner aims material at named speakers) and YED-218 (question claim type) were filed to merge, and they matter MORE after this result, not less.
consequences: Graph-write freeze LIFTS — measurement is complete. It lifts on the experiment finishing, not on a particular verdict.
YED-47 (identity S1b-lite) and YED-205 (pre-event write path) unblock.
ADR-10 stays Proposed. Do not mark Accepted.
The substrate is NOT retired — it is re-scoped: it stays the post-event claim store and the job-search/interview lens, and the open question becomes coverage, not method.
honest_caveats: Event 1 was dropped after being run, which is a mid-experiment change of the sample.
Apollo required a decontamination deviation; AI Builders did not.
Confounds on the Apollo run favoured the legacy arm on balance (hand-written keyword list for its signal sweep, residual batch-window leak) — so the legacy win is if anything slightly overstated.
